requirements.requirement: Configure node1 to boot with audit=1 and preserve the setting across reboots.
requirements.summary: The persistent GRUB source was set to audit=1 and all three generated Linux entries included it. A bounded reboot changed the boot ID; afterward, /proc/cmdline contained audit=1, the system was running with a writable root filesystem, the persistent GRUB setting remained present, and kernel messages reported audit_enabled=1.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel, using only platform-compatible software.
requirements.summary: Before and after the change and reboot, node1 remained on Ubuntu 24.04 with kernel 6.8.0-71-generic. No software installation, release upgrade, or kernel replacement occurred in the command timeline; the existing GRUB tooling was used.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied. The restart protocol is strong for the single managed node: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart scheduling acknowledgement, a different post-restart boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered system, filesystem, persistent configuration, OS, and kernel state.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Editing the persistent GRUB setting and regenerating grub.cfg directly implemented the requested outcome; creating /tmp/grub.before-audit was a bounded rollback safeguard and it did not remain after reboot; scheduling the single reboot was required to verify persistence. Post-executor observations show no failed services, package damage, or unexpected lasting exposure. Socket and systemd-private temporary-file differences are ordinary reboot effects.
